pairs.evidence: src/app/api/org/decision/route.ts:9 The route promises a decision is reversible, but decide() writes nothing to Shared Org Memory on reopen and never retires or supersedes the row it published, and activeMemoryWhere filters only archived, superseded and expired rows, so connected agents keep recalling a ruling the human has withdrawn until episodic decay removes it.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/org-decisions.ts:242 A human reversal is the highest-grade correction, yet it is neither remembered as an event nor superseding: no memory write happens on status open, and no code reads OrgDecision.memoryId to retire the earlier row.

src/lib/db/org-decisions.ts:246 The decision is state-valued on the code-owned key (orgId, module, itemKey), but re-deciding mints a new live row without supersedeId, which createOrgMemory supports (org-memory.ts:398), so accepted and dismissed versions of one ruling stay live side by side.

src/lib/db/org-decisions.ts:226 The snooze states its own validity boundary, but the memory call passes no expiresAt and the content omits the date, so a lapsed snooze is still recited; only the 30-day episodic half-life limits it, and the technique says a half-life cannot substitute for an expiry.
src/lib/db/org-decisions.ts:245 Admission to memory is decided in code by the lifecycle field rather than inferred from prose, and the status is carried into the row's content and tags.

src/lib/db/org-decisions.ts:201 One record per human ruling, closed on a real event, with a one-sentence body holding outcome, actor and reason. The raw-source pointer runs only from the decision row to the memory, not back.

src/app/api/org/decision/route.ts:57 The memory is owned by the gated org and the author is passed separately as createdBy, so owner is not conflated with writer; no counterpart axis arises on this path.
